case_label: Stage IV colorectal cancer, KRAS G12C, partial response to FOLFOX/bev
synthetic_disclaimer: All identifiers, dates, and clinical details are fictional. Constructed for hackathon demo purposes; not based on any real patient.
demographics: 58M, ECOG 1. PMHx: hypertension on lisinopril, hyperlipidemia on atorvastatin. Former smoker (quit 2014, 15 pack-years). Body mass index 29. Works in construction, currently on medical leave. Wife is primary support. No family history of colorectal cancer. Last colonoscopy at age 50 was normal.
diagnosis: Adenocarcinoma of the sigmoid colon with synchronous liver metastases. Stage IV (cT3 cN2 M1) at diagnosis November 2025. Microsatellite stable, KRAS G12C mutation, BRAF wild type, MMR proficient.
pathology: Sigmoid biopsy (Nov 2025): Moderately differentiated invasive adenocarcinoma, intestinal type. CK20 positive, CDX2 positive, CK7 negative. MMR by IHC: MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2 all retained — MMR proficient. Liver biopsy, segment VI (Nov 2025): Metastatic adenocarcinoma, immunoprofile consistent with colorectal primary.
molecular: Tissue NGS (sigmoid biopsy, November 2025): KRAS G12C mutation. APC truncating mutation. TP53 mutation. SMAD4 mutation. BRAF wild type. MSI-stable by PCR. TMB 7 mut/Mb. HER2 not amplified. NTRK fusions not detected. ctDNA panel (April 2026, on therapy): KRAS G12C detectable at low VAF (0.4%, down from 6.1% at baseline). APC and TP53 likewise lower. No new alterations.
imaging: Baseline CT chest/abdomen/pelvis (Nov 2025): 5.2 cm sigmoid mass with regional lymphadenopathy. Multiple bilobar liver lesions, largest 4.1 cm in segment VII, additional lesions in segments IV, V, VI, VIII (5 total lesions). No lung or peritoneal disease. Restaging CT (April 22, 2026): After 8 cycles of FOLFOX + bevacizumab. Sigmoid mass decreased to 3.0 cm. Liver — segment VII lesion now 1.8 cm (from 4.1), segment V lesion 0.9 cm (from 2.0), three other lesions <8 mm or no longer measurable. RECIST 1.1: partial response. No new lesions. CEA April 25: 14.2 (peak baseline 287, nadir 11.8 last cycle).
treatment_timeline:
- Nov 2025: Diagnosed stage IV sigmoid adenocarcinoma with bilobar liver mets. KRAS G12C, MSS.
- Dec 2025 - April 2026: First-line FOLFOX + bevacizumab, 8 cycles completed. Tolerating with grade 1-2 neuropathy and grade 1 fatigue. Bevacizumab held cycle 5 for transient hypertension, resumed.
- April 2026: Restaging — partial response by RECIST. Currently on cycle 9 hold pending board discussion of locoregional therapy options.
current_status_summary: Patient feels significantly better than at diagnosis — appetite returned, weight stable, less abdominal cramping. Mild persistent peripheral neuropathy in fingertips and toes (grade 1, no functional impact). No bowel obstruction symptoms. ECOG 1 (down from 2 at diagnosis). Recent labs (April 25): Hgb 12.1 (was 9.8 pre-treatment), platelets 168, ANC 2.2, AST 32, ALT 28, ALP 96, total bilirubin 0.7, albumin 4.0, creatinine 1.0. CEA 14.2 (down from 287 baseline). Urine protein/creatinine ratio normal.
clinical_question: Optimal sequencing of locoregional and systemic therapy in a partial responder to first-line FOLFOX + bevacizumab with KRAS G12C-mutant MSS metastatic colorectal cancer. Specifically: (1) is this patient now a candidate for hepatic resection with or without simultaneous primary resection, given the response and reduction in liver burden, (2) role of bridge to surgery with continued chemotherapy versus consolidation with KRAS G12C inhibitor combination on a clinical trial, (3) if surgery is pursued, recommended interval off bevacizumab pre-operatively, (4) post-operative systemic therapy sequence and duration.
